verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew returned to Earth on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: URL '2026/04/10/science/nasa-artemis-ii-splashdown-return', 'on Friday' after April 1 launch; R3: 'April 10, 2026 in Downey, California'; R5: 'on Friday' with URL '2026/04/10/science/nasa-artemis-ii-splash-down'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly reference April 10, 2026, as the splashdown date via URLs and explicit mentions.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew had a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown... at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time... waters off San Diego'; R2: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT'; R3: 'splashed down off San Diego... at 7:07 p.m. CST' (equiv to 8:07 EDT)
verifications.reasoning: Exact location and time match across sources.

verifications.claim: 8:07 p.m. EDT is equivalent to 5:07 p.m. PDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'approximate 10-day mission'; R3: 'nearly 10-day mission'; R4: 'record-breaking 10-day mission' but precise '9 days, 1 hour'; R5: 'after 10 days'; R6: '10-day journey'
verifications.reasoning: Broadly described as 10-day mission, though precise duration is ~9 days 1 hour; supported in general terms.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission was the first crewed flight to orbit the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first people to leave low-Earth orbit since 1972', 'lunar flyby', 'swung around the moon’s far side'; no mention of orbiting the Moon
verifications.reasoning: Mission was a lunar flyby, not orbit; sources describe flyby/around Moon, contradicting 'orbit the Moon' (last was Apollo 17, 1972).

verifications.claim: The Artemis II entry interface occurred at 7:53 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'At 7:53 p.m.... “entry interface”'; R2: '7:53 p.m. The Orion spacecraft reached Earth’s atmosphere'; R4: 'entry interface," began at 7:53 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and term directly stated.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II splashdown time was 8:07 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8:07 p.m. Eastern time'; R2: '8:07 p.m. EDT'; R4: '8:07 p.m. ET'; R5: '8:07 p.m. Eastern time'; R6: '8:07 p.m. ET'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II splashdown location was the Pacific Ocean west of San Diego.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Pacific Ocean... waters off San Diego'; R2: 'Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'off San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Directly 'off the coast of San Diego' in Pacific (west); precise 'west' implied by geography.
